title: System Databases
description: Learn about the SQL Server system databases and their purposes.

data.text: By default, SQL Server provides four main system databases that are essential for the operation of the SQL Server instance.

The master database stores all system-level information of an SQL Server instance, including server configuration settings, logon accounts, linked servers information, startup stored procedures, and file locations of user databases.

data.title: Critical
data.text: If the master database is unavailable, SQL Server cannot start. Always have a current backup of the master database.

items: Always have a current backup of the master database.
Back up the master database after creating, modifying, or dropping any database.
Do not create user objects in the master database.
Do not set the TRUSTWORTHY database property of master to ON.

data.text: The msdb database is used by SQL Server Agent for scheduling jobs and alerts. It also stores the history of SQL Agent jobs, supports Database Mail, Service Broker, and backup/restore history.

The model database serves as a template for creating other databases. When you create a new database, SQL Server copies the contents of the model database including database options. If you modify the model database, all databases created afterward will take these changes.

The tempdb database stores temporary user objects like temporary tables and table variables. It also stores internal objects created by the database engine, such as immediate sort results for queries with ORDER BY clauses. SQL Server recreates tempdb every time it starts, so you cannot back it up or restore it.

data.title: System Databases Key Points
points: master stores system-level information and is critical for SQL Server startup.
msdb supports SQL Server Agent jobs, alerts, and backup history.
model is the template for creating new databases.
tempdb stores temporary objects and is recreated on every server start.
Never create user objects in the master database.
